title: Native NNA settings coverage working census

conventions.wildcards: [*] denotes native identity-bearing array entries; {name} denotes validated dynamic map keys, not arbitrary accepted properties.
conventions.unknown: unverified or null means not established; every row remains open.
conventions.evidence: Source inspection only. No test execution or installed GUI effect is claimed.
conventions.containers: Containers and leaves are separate structural rows; row count is not editable setting count.
conventions.scope: Manifest layers are resolver sources, not proof each field is admitted in each context.
conventions.apply: Only explicit consumer evidence establishes apply class. General runtime acceptance does not prove hot application.
conventions.secrets: Never place secret values in this ledger.
conventions.classification: Manifest-family kind values must equal the NNA classified catalog classification for the same structural path; invocation rows describe accepted CLI option literals from the two NNA option modules. scripts/settings-coverage-gate.mjs enforces both directions and rejects unclassified additions.

remaining_census: All repository environment reads, dynamic credentials, CLI positional subcommands and TUI commands.
Full secret create/update/scope schema and per-field validation, references and binding lifecycle.
On-disk skill formats and native install/remove/edit action availability; current skills CLI only lists.
Nested telemetry retention, route budgets/fallbacks, MCP effects; per-field bounds/default/null/reset/apply consumers.
NNO activation, full installation/startup/discovery schemas and evolving L2 contracts.
Cross-check operator docs, endpoint permissions, UI controls and tests.
Extend the C1 gate beyond dashed CLI options and the classified manifest catalog to positional subcommands, environment reads, and non-manifest stores.

known_mismatches.issue: MCP editor writes OpenCode configuration, not NNA configuration.
Integration user-manifest resolution differs from layered startup resolver.
Legacy helper resolution reads /config/providers and OpenCode auth.json.

rows.notes: the service always projects the re-verified descriptor on GET /v1/nnd/configuration/installation (nnd.configuration.read): the read re-runs the admission authority (readNndServiceIdentity — descriptor validation, canonicalization, payload and runtime checks) and fails closed when the disk no longer supports the admitted installation (nnd_install_* surfaced verbatim at 503; a projected value the router cannot accept is the 500 nnd_installation_projection_invalid), so the operator repairs the installation instead of the listener projecting a lost admission; registered failure codes now surface verbatim from the configuration router (registered = safe to surface). The desktop panel (NNA installation) renders product, version, install root, data root, and the node runtime; the -3 environment page shows only the manifest ownership identity (no installer state), so it is not this family's GUI.

rows.notes: NND console consumes the runtime SecretBroker verbatim (dispatchSecretBrokerRequest over the integration server): the roster renders the redacted publicSecret records only - labels, kinds, scopes, field NAMES, enablement, use counts, never a value - and mutations send typed field values ONCE (create POST /v1/secrets, rotate PUT /v1/secrets/:id/values, update PATCH label/scope/metadata with no values, enable/disable PATCH /v1/secrets/:id/status, delete DELETE /v1/secrets/:id), each returning the broker redacted receipt; the audit view reads GET /v1/secrets/audit whose events carry no values; there is deliberately no client for POST /v1/secrets/:id/use - consumption stays with trusted local callers holding secret.use, which the NND operator principal never carries; permissions ride the principal (secret.read/list + secret.manage mutations + secret.audit audit view) Closed 20261007-23 on evidence. Shown: the roster itself, one row per record with label, kind, scope and field names, and every value withheld. The pin came from before C1: its only citation was a bulk suite count, the whole vitest run named as proof of one field, which proves nothing about this row even when the number is honest, and it carried no application evidence at all. Reading the actual console test is what confirmed the claim rather than contradicting it, worth saying plainly since other pre-C1 pins did not survive the same look. The class word is NNA (next_secret_use) rather than a desktop coinage, and where a verb is a pure read the row says not_applied instead of borrowing the effect claim. Sensitivity stays secret as the vault family sets it.

apply.evidence: src/secret-broker-server.js routes this verb straight to the runtime SecretBroker over the integration server, where values are stored encrypted and only metadata projects; the effect lands when a trusted consumer next reads the vault, which is when NNA hands values over transiently with exact-value redaction active. The word next_secret_use is NNA (src/nnd-secrets-routes.js declares it for this same vault, and POST /v1/secrets/:id/use is the use event itself); the broker has no catalog of its own, and this console never calls that endpoint, so it never fabricates a use
